Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Yokozuna: A yokozuna wears a thick white rope at ceremonies and cannot be demoted. When his performance fades, he is expected to retire.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Ozeki: Unlike the grand champion, an ozeki can be demoted, but if he loses a tournament he gets a second chance to keep the rank.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Sekiwake: Normally two wrestlers hold this rank, one east and one west, and a strong record here is a stepping stone toward ozeki.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Komusubi: The lowest of the three titled ranks below yokozuna, komusubi means 'small connection' and brings bouts against the stars.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Maegashira: Most top-division wrestlers are maegashira, numbered from 1 down to about 17, and a strong run can lift them into the titled ranks.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Juryo: Juryo wrestlers are the first to draw a salary, and they get a silk belt and personal attendants.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Makushita: Below this rank wrestlers receive only small stipends, and it takes its name from a word meaning 'below the curtain'.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Sandanme: Sandanme means 'third level', and wrestlers here fight just seven bouts per tournament, not the fifteen of the top divisions.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Jonidan: The second-lowest of the six divisions, where young wrestlers fight seven bouts per tournament.
Sumo ranks, from the top of the banzuke.Jonokuchi: The name means 'mouth of the start', and new recruits begin here, fighting only a handful of bouts at a time.

Landmark hip-hop releases.Rapper's Delight: The Sugarhill Gang's single was the first hip-hop song to reach the Top 40, built on a bassline borrowed from Chic's 'Good Times'.
Landmark hip-hop releases.Licensed to Ill: The Beastie Boys' debut was the first rap album to reach number one on the Billboard 200.
Landmark hip-hop releases.Straight Outta Compton: NWA's debut helped launch gangsta rap, and 'F Tha Police' drew a warning letter from the FBI.
Landmark hip-hop releases.The Chronic: Dr. Dre's solo debut introduced Snoop Dogg to the world and defined the smooth sound called G-funk.
Landmark hip-hop releases.Illmatic: Nas was only 20 when he made it, and its ten tracks are often called the best of hip-hop.
Landmark hip-hop releases.Miseducation of Lauryn Hill: Lauryn Hill won five Grammys in a single night for it, a record for a female artist.
Landmark hip-hop releases.The Marshall Mathers LP: Eminem's album sold about 1.7 million copies in its first week, then a record for a solo artist.
Landmark hip-hop releases.The College Dropout: Kanye West had produced for Jay-Z before this debut, and he rapped 'Through the Wire' with his jaw wired shut after a car crash.
Landmark hip-hop releases.good kid, m.A.A.d city: Kendrick Lamar's cinematic album about growing up in Compton carries the subtitle 'A Short Film'.
It became the first work outside classical and jazz to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music, in 2018.

Milestones in understanding the Earth.Hutton's deep time: James Hutton saw layered rocks at Siccar Point and declared he found 'no vestige of a beginning', so Earth is immeasurably old.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.William Smith's geologic map: This canal engineer made the first geological map of England and Wales, using fossils to identify rock layers.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Agassiz's ice ages: The Swiss-born scientist argued glaciers once covered Europe, based on scratched rocks and moraines.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Mohorovičić discontinuity: This Croatian seismologist spotted a boundary between crust and mantle from earthquake waves; it is known as the Moho.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Lehmann's inner core: Danish seismologist Inge Lehmann deduced the solid inner core from seismic waves.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Patterson dates Earth: Clair Patterson dated Earth from lead isotopes in a meteorite, finding about 4.55 billion years.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Keeling Curve begins: Charles Keeling measured carbon dioxide atop Mauna Loa, showing its steady annual rise.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Hess: seafloor spreading: Harry Hess proposed new crust forms at mid-ocean ridges and spreads, helping lay the groundwork for plate tectonics.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Alvarez asteroid theory: Luis and Walter Alvarez linked an iridium-rich layer to an asteroid impact that killed the dinosaurs.
Milestones in understanding the Earth.Chicxulub crater identified: The crater, about 180 km wide and buried under Yucatan, was tied to the dinosaur-killing impact.

Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Standard Oil: John D. Rockefeller founded it in 1870, and it was broken up in 1911 into companies including Exxon and Mobil.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Royal Dutch Shell: It was the 1907 merger of Royal Dutch and Shell Transport; Shell began as a seashell trading business.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Anglo-Persian Oil (BP): Founded in 1909 after William D'Arcy found oil in Persia in 1908, it was later renamed BP.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Total (as CFP): The French government pushed for a national oil company in 1924, and it later became TotalEnergies.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Aramco (as CASOC): CASOC was formed in 1933 by Standard Oil of California, and oil was found at Dammam in 1938.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Pemex: Created in 1938 after Mexico nationalised foreign oil companies, an event still celebrated.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Petrobras: Created after the 1953 campaign O petroleo e nosso, it is Brazil's state oil giant.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.OPEC: Founded in Baghdad in 1960 by five countries: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela; it is now based in Vienna.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Statoil (Equinor): Norway's state oil company, founded after North Sea discoveries, was renamed Equinor in 2018.
Oil and energy giants, by founding year.Gazprom: Created in 1989 from the Soviet Ministry of Gas, it is one of the largest gas producers.

Artificial body parts through history.Cairo wooden toe: The Cairo toe is a wooden and leather big toe found on a mummy, and it may have actually helped its owner walk.
Artificial body parts through history.Capua bronze leg: The Capua leg was a bronze and wood prosthetic, and it was found in a tomb in Italy, and a replica was made to test it.
Artificial body parts through history.Götz's iron hand: Gotz von Berlichingen's iron hand had movable fingers, and he was a knight who inspired Goethe's play.
Artificial body parts through history.Hanger's artificial leg: James Hanger invented an artificial leg after losing his own in the American Civil War, and his company still exists.
Artificial body parts through history.Electric hearing aid: The electric hearing aid arrived with Alexander Graham Bell's circle, and early models were bulky tabletop devices.
Artificial body parts through history.Multichannel cochlear implant: Cochlear implants bypass damaged parts of the ear and send signals to the auditory nerve, and many deaf children now get them.
Artificial body parts through history.Jarvik-7 artificial heart: The Jarvik-7 artificial heart was implanted in Barney Clark, who lived 112 days, and it was a landmark in transplant medicine.
Artificial body parts through history.Flex-Foot blade: The Flex-Foot blade is a curved carbon-fiber prosthesis, and it was invented by Van Phillips, who lost a leg in a water-skiing accident.
Artificial body parts through history.Argus II bionic eye approved: The Argus II was the first bionic eye approved, and it gave people with certain blindness the ability to see light patterns.
Artificial body parts through history.Neuralink's first human: Neuralink implanted its first human brain chip in January 2024, and the patient was able to move a cursor with thought.

When these chess greats were born.Paul Morphy: The American prodigy beat Europe's best before retiring young, and is often called the unofficial world champion.
When these chess greats were born.Jose Raul Capablanca: Nicknamed the human chess machine, the Cuban champion barely lost a game for years.
When these chess greats were born.Mikhail Botvinnik: The Soviet patriarch of chess trained Karpov, Kasparov and Kramnik, and was an electrical engineer.
When these chess greats were born.Bobby Fischer: He beat Boris Spassky in 1972 in Reykjavik, a Cold War showdown that made chess front-page news.
When these chess greats were born.Anatoly Karpov: He became world champion in 1975 when Fischer refused to defend his title, and then kept it for ten years.
When these chess greats were born.Garry Kasparov: He lost to IBM's Deep Blue in 1997, after having become the youngest undisputed champion at 22.
When these chess greats were born.Viswanathan Anand: The Tiger of Madras, from India, was world champion from 2007 to 2013, and inspired a generation.
When these chess greats were born.Judit Polgar: She became a grandmaster at 15, the youngest then, and she beat Kasparov in a rapid game in 2002.
When these chess greats were born.Magnus Carlsen: A grandmaster at 13, he held the classical world title from 2013 to 2023 and reached the highest rating ever recorded.
When these chess greats were born.Gukesh Dommaraju: At 18, he became the youngest ever world champion by beating Ding Liren in 2024.

Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Rosh Hashanah: Jewish New Year is marked by blowing the shofar, a ram's horn, and eating apples with honey for a sweet year.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Yom Kippur: The Day of Atonement is the holiest day of the year, observed with a fast of about 25 hours and prayer.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Sukkot: People eat in a temporary hut called a sukkah, recalling the Israelites' wandering in the desert.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Simchat Torah: The annual Torah reading cycle ends and begins again, celebrated with dancing with the scrolls.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Hanukkah: This eight-night festival of lights commemorates a rededicated Temple and oil that lasted eight days.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Tu BiShvat: The New Year for trees is often marked by eating fruits and planting trees in Israel.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Purim: Purim recalls Queen Esther saving the Jews of Persia, with the Megillah read aloud and people dressing up and giving gifts.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Passover: The seder recalls the exodus from Egypt, and matzah is eaten because the Israelites left without time for bread to rise.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Shavuot: It marks the giving of the Torah at Sinai, and many eat dairy foods such as cheesecake.
Jewish holidays, from the start of the y.Tisha B'Av: This fast day mourns the destruction of both Temples in Jerusalem, along with other disasters.

Mountain animals by weight.American pika: The pika doesn't hibernate; it gathers grass into haypiles for winter. It lives high in the Rockies and is so heat-sensitive that it can die in warm weather.
Mountain animals by weight.Alpine chough: This relative of crows lives higher than almost any bird, and has been seen at over 8,000 m on Everest, scavenging from climbers' camps.
Mountain animals by weight.Chinchilla: Chinchillas have the densest fur of any land mammal, with up to about 60 hairs per follicle, which is why they take dust baths rather than water ones.
Mountain animals by weight.Himalayan marmot: Himalayan marmots hibernate for roughly half the year in deep burrows, and they live on high alpine meadows, often above 3,500 m.
Mountain animals by weight.Andean condor: A national bird of several Andean countries, it has a wingspan of up to about 3 m and can glide for hours without flapping.
Mountain animals by weight.Snow leopard: Snow leopards can leap about 15 m, and use their long tail, almost as long as their body, for balance and as a scarf to cover the nose.
Mountain animals by weight.Alpine ibex (male): Males carry sweeping curved horns that can top a meter, and the species was brought back from fewer than 100 animals in Italy's Gran Paradiso.
Mountain animals by weight.Spectacled bear: South America's only bear is named for the pale rings around its eyes, and it is a mostly vegetarian climber that builds treetop platforms.
Mountain animals by weight.Takin: This stocky goat-antelope from the eastern Himalayas is Bhutan's national animal, and its odd looks led some to call it a gnu-goat.
Mountain animals by weight.Wild yak: Wild yaks live above 4,000 m on the Tibetan Plateau, with huge lungs and hearts, and thick coats that let them survive temperatures near -40 degrees.

Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Antoninus Pius: Antoninus Pius ruled peacefully for 23 years, and his reign is often seen as a golden age of Rome, with the Antonine Wall built in Scotland.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Marcus Aurelius: Marcus Aurelius wrote the Meditations, a book of Stoic thoughts, in the midst of wars and plague, and ruled as a philosopher-emperor.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Commodus: Commodus, portrayed in the film Gladiator, fought in the arena himself and was strangled in his bath in 192.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Septimius Severus: Septimius Severus was born in Africa, and was the first emperor from North Africa, and he died in York, Britain, while campaigning.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Caracalla: Caracalla granted Roman citizenship to nearly all free people in the empire and built huge baths in Rome that are still standing.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Aurelian: Aurelian reunited the empire after its crisis and built walls around Rome that still stand in many places.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Diocletian: Diocletian split the empire into east and west with co-rulers, and retired to grow cabbages in his palace in modern Croatia.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Constantine the Great: Constantine legalized Christianity, moved the capital to Constantinople, and is said to have seen a cross in the sky before a battle.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Julian the Apostate: Julian was the last pagan emperor and tried to restore the old gods, and the Christians called him 'the Apostate'.
Later Roman emperors, by start of reign.Romulus Augustulus: Romulus Augustulus, a teenager, was deposed by Odoacer, which traditionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire.

When these towers were completed.Leaning Tower of Pisa: The tilt began during construction because one side sat on soft clay, and engineers straightened it a little in the 1990s and 2001.
When these towers were completed.Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben): Big Ben is strictly the great bell inside, not the tower, which was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for the Queen's Diamond Jubilee.
When these towers were completed.Washington Monument: Look closely and the stone changes color about a third of the way up, because building stalled for years during funding troubles and the Civil War.
When these towers were completed.Eiffel Tower: Meant to stand just 20 years as a World's Fair exhibit, it was saved from demolition by its usefulness as a radio antenna.
When these towers were completed.Blackpool Tower: Modeled on the Eiffel Tower, it rises from a building that houses a ballroom and a circus.
When these towers were completed.Space Needle: It was built in about 400 days for the Seattle World's Fair, whose theme looked ahead to the 21st century.
When these towers were completed.Berlin TV Tower: When sunlight hits its steel dome it throws a cross, which Berliners nicknamed the Pope's Revenge.
When these towers were completed.CN Tower: It was the world's tallest free-standing structure for more than 30 years, until the Burj Khalifa overtook it.
When these towers were completed.Canton Tower: The twisted lattice shape earned it the nickname Slim Waist, and it is shaped as a hyperboloid.
When these towers were completed.Tokyo Skytree: Its height of about 634 meters was chosen because 6-3-4 reads as Musashi, the old name of the region around Tokyo.

Old as the hills: which happened first?.Earth forms: It coalesced from a disc of gas and dust around the young Sun, and a Mars-sized body, Theia, is thought to have hit it and thrown off the Moon.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.First life appears: The oldest candidate traces are microbial; single-celled organisms ruled the planet for billions of years before anything larger appeared.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Oxygen fills the air: Cyanobacteria's photosynthesis released the oxygen, a Great Oxidation Event that wiped out many microbes that could not tolerate it.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Plants move onto land: These first land plants were small, mossy things like liverworts, but their roots began breaking rock into soil.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Pangaea assembles: Pangaea means all earth in Greek, and a single ocean, Panthalassa, surrounded the supercontinent.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Dinosaurs die out: An asteroid struck near Chicxulub in Mexico, but birds, living descendants of dinosaurs, survived it.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Grand Canyon carved: The Colorado River cut the canyon, yet the rocks at its bottom are up to about 1.8 billion years old, far older than the canyon itself.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Last ice age ends: As the ice melted, sea levels rose by roughly 120 meters, drowning land bridges such as the one joining Britain to Europe.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Pompeii buried: Ash from Vesuvius sealed the city so completely that archaeologists have found loaves of bread, graffiti and even body-shaped voids.
Old as the hills: which happened first?.Mount St. Helens blows: The eruption killed 57 people and shaved roughly 400 meters off the summit, making it the deadliest volcanic event in US history.

How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Mayfly (adult): Adults have no working mouth and exist only to mate, after a juvenile stage underwater that can last a year or more.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Housefly: A female can lay hundreds of eggs in a few batches, which is why they multiply so quickly in warm weather.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Hamster: Every pet golden hamster descends from a single litter caught in Syria in 1930.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.House cat: Creme Puff, the oldest cat on record, reached 38.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Horse: The oldest horse on record, Old Billy, lived to 62.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Human (global average): Global life expectancy has more than doubled since 1900, when it was about 32 years.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Galapagos tortoise: Lonesome George, the last of his subspecies, died in 2012 at about 100 years old, still young for his kind.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Bowhead whale: Harpoon tips from the 1800s have been found embedded in living bowheads, evidence of their extreme longevity.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Greenland shark: They grow only around a centimeter a year and may not reach maturity until about 150 years old.
How long they can live, mayfly to ancien.Methuselah bristlecone pine: Growing in California's White Mountains, its exact location is kept secret to protect it.

Fashion houses, by founding year.Hermès: The house began making horse harnesses, and the Birkin bag is named for actress Jane Birkin.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Louis Vuitton: It started as a Paris trunk maker, and its monogram canvas dates to 1896 as a defense against imitators.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Burberry: Thomas Burberry invented gabardine, the weatherproof cloth behind the trench coat worn in World War I.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Chanel: Coco Chanel popularized the little black dress and the tweed suit, and made comfort fashionable for women.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Prada: It began as a Milan luxury leather goods shop founded by Mario Prada, and later became famous for nylon bags.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Gucci: Guccio Gucci worked as a hotel porter in London before founding the house, inspired by the luggage of rich guests.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Dior: Christian Dior's 1947 'New Look' reshaped fashion after the war with its nipped waist and full skirts.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Ralph Lauren: He began by selling ties under the Polo name, building a lifestyle empire from a single product.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Versace: Gianni Versace chose the Greek Medusa as the house's emblem, and the brand became famous for bold, glamorous prints.
Fashion houses, by founding year.Supreme: This New York skate shop turned a red box logo into a streetwear icon, with collaborations ranging from Louis Vuitton to crowbars.

Great astronomers, by birth year.Ptolemy: Ptolemy worked in Roman Alexandria, and his Earth-centered model stood for about 1,400 years, while he also wrote on geography and optics.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Nicolaus Copernicus: He proposed the Sun-centered model, published in 1543, and legend says he saw the first printed copy on his deathbed.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Tycho Brahe: He lost part of his nose in a duel and wore a metal replacement, yet made the most precise naked-eye measurements.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Galileo Galilei: With a telescope he saw Jupiter's moons and Venus's phases; the Inquisition forced him to recant and live under house arrest.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Johannes Kepler: Using Tycho's data, he found planets move in ellipses, not circles, and his laws guided Newton.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Edmond Halley: He predicted the comet's return, and also funded and edited Newton's Principia.
Great astronomers, by birth year.William Herschel: Born in Hanover, he discovered Uranus and infrared radiation, with help from his sister Caroline.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Edwin Hubble: He showed Andromeda is a separate galaxy and that the universe is expanding, and a space telescope bears his name.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Carl Sagan: He hosted the TV series Cosmos, helped choose the Voyager Golden Record, and suggested the Pale Blue Dot photo.
Great astronomers, by birth year.Stephen Hawking: Diagnosed with ALS at 21, he predicted black holes emit radiation, now called Hawking radiation, and wrote A Brief History of Time.

European countries by area.Luxembourg: Europe's last grand duchy has three official languages, Luxembourgish, French and German, and ranks among the world's richest per person.
European countries by area.Belgium: Brussels hosts the main EU institutions, and the country has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
European countries by area.Switzerland: Not an EU member, it has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
European countries by area.Portugal: Its border with Spain has barely changed since the Treaty of Alcañices in 1297, among the oldest in Europe.
European countries by area.United Kingdom: It consists of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, and its only land border is with Ireland.
European countries by area.Italy: The boot-shaped country completely surrounds two tiny enclaves: San Marino and Vatican City.
European countries by area.Germany: It borders nine other countries, the most of any country entirely in the EU.
European countries by area.Sweden: It has about 100,000 lakes, and long summer nights north of the Arctic Circle bring the midnight sun.
European countries by area.Spain: The EU's second-largest country by area has about 50 UNESCO World Heritage sites.
European countries by area.Ukraine: It is the largest country lying entirely within Europe, bigger than metropolitan France.

When these body parts named after people.Fallopian tubes: Named for Gabriele Falloppio, the Italian anatomist who described the tubes that carry eggs.
When these body parts named after people.Peyer's patches: These patches of immune tissue in the small intestine are named after Johann Conrad Peyer.
When these body parts named after people.Haversian canals: These microscopic channels in compact bone are named for Clopton Havers.
When these body parts named after people.Purkinje fibers: These specialized muscle fibers in the heart are named after the Czech physiologist Jan Purkinje.
When these body parts named after people.Broca's area: This brain region involved in speech production was described by Paul Broca after studying a patient who could say only one word.
When these body parts named after people.Islets of Langerhans: These cell clusters in the pancreas make insulin and are named for Paul Langerhans, who found them as a student.
When these body parts named after people.Wernicke's area: This brain area is involved in understanding language, and it's named for Carl Wernicke.
When these body parts named after people.Bundle of His: This bundle of fibers carries signals in the heart, and it's named for Swiss cardiologist Wilhelm His Jr.
When these body parts named after people.Golgi apparatus: Camillo Golgi discovered this cell structure that packages proteins, and he won a Nobel Prize in 1906.
When these body parts named after people.Krebs cycle: Hans Krebs described this cycle that releases energy from food in cells, and he won a Nobel Prize for it in 1953.

Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Absolute zero: Absolute zero is the coldest temperature possible, and no object has ever been cooled to precisely this level.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Coldest Antarctic record: The lowest air temperature measured on Earth was recorded at Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Human body: Normal body temperature is about 37 °C, and it varies slightly through the day.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Boiling water: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level, and at the top of Everest it boils at about 70 °C.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Wood-fired pizza oven: Traditional wood-fired pizza ovens run at roughly this heat, and a pizza cooks in only a minute or two.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Flowing lava: Lava flows are hot enough to melt many metals, and the temperature varies with the type of volcano.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Iron melting point: Iron melts at this temperature, and ancient smiths reached it using bellows and charcoal.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Surface of the Sun: The Sun's surface is far cooler than its core, and its color is about the temperature of white light.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.A lightning bolt: Lightning heats the air to about five times the Sun's surface temperature, and the sudden expansion makes thunder.
Temperature: from deep freeze to star co.Core of the Sun: The Sun's core fuses hydrogen into helium, which is what keeps it shining for billions of years.

When these rules came in.Forward pass in US football: President Theodore Roosevelt pushed for reform after a series of deaths in the brutal early game, and the pass opened the sport up.
When these rules came in.NBA shot clock: Danny Biasone worked out 24 seconds by dividing the game's 48 minutes by 120 shots. It ended games as dull as a 19-18 score.
When these rules came in.Yellow and red cards: English referee Ken Aston thought of them while stopped at a traffic light, and they debuted at the 1970 World Cup.
When these rules came in.Designated hitter (AL): It let a bat replace the pitcher in the lineup. The National League held out until 2022 before adopting it too.
When these rules came in.NBA three-point line: The rival ABA had used the line earlier, and the NBA copied it. Chris Ford of the Celtics made the first one.
When these rules came in.3 points for a win (England): It was meant to reward attacking play, and FIFA brought it to the World Cup in 1994.
When these rules came in.Soccer back-pass rule: Goalkeepers can no longer pick up a deliberate pass from teammates, a change that came after time-wasting at the 1990 World Cup.
When these rules came in.Hawk-Eye at Wimbledon: The camera system let players challenge line calls, and tracks the ball's flight to within a few millimetres.
When these rules came in.VAR at the World Cup: Russia 2018 was the first World Cup with video referees, and the first with a penalty awarded after a video review.
When these rules came in.MLB pitch clock: Pitchers must deliver within a set time, and it trimmed the average game by around 25 minutes.

How long it takes in your body.One blink: You blink about 15 to 20 times a minute, but far less when staring at a screen.
How long it takes in your body.One heartbeat: At rest, your heart beats about 100,000 times a day.
How long it takes in your body.Swallowed food to stomach: Waves of muscle contraction called peristalsis push food down, even if you're upside-down.
How long it takes in your body.Stomach emptying a meal: Fatty meals take longer, since fat slows the stomach's emptying.
How long it takes in your body.Life of a taste bud: Taste buds replace about every 10 days, which is why a burnt tongue recovers quickly.
How long it takes in your body.Skin surface renewing: Its outer layer is made of dead cells, which you constantly shed.
How long it takes in your body.Life of a red blood cell: They are broken down in the spleen, and bone marrow makes about two million new ones every second.
How long it takes in your body.Regrowing a fingernail: Fingernails grow about 3 mm a month, so a lost one takes around half a year.
How long it takes in your body.Regrowing a toenail: Toenails grow roughly three times slower than fingernails, hence the wait.
How long it takes in your body.Renewing your skeleton: Bone is constantly remodeled by specialized cells, so an adult's whole skeleton is renewed about every decade.

Operas, by premiere year.L'Orfeo: Monteverdi's work from 1607 is the oldest opera still regularly performed.
Operas, by premiere year.Don Giovanni: Mozart's opera about the legendary seducer premiered in Prague, with a libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte.
Operas, by premiere year.The Magic Flute: It premiered just weeks before Mozart's death, and contains the Queen of the Night's famously high arias.
Operas, by premiere year.The Barber of Seville: Rossini's comic masterpiece had a chaotic opening night, with a cat reportedly wandering onto the stage.
Operas, by premiere year.La traviata: Verdi's opera is based on Dumas fils's novel The Lady of the Camellias.
Operas, by premiere year.Carmen: Bizet's opera got a lukewarm reception at its premiere, and he died three months later.
Operas, by premiere year.La bohème: Puccini's tale of poor artists in Paris inspired the musical Rent.
Operas, by premiere year.Madama Butterfly: Puccini's opera flopped at its La Scala premiere, then was revised and became a hit.
Operas, by premiere year.Porgy and Bess: Gershwin's opera is set in Charleston and features the lullaby 'Summertime'.
Operas, by premiere year.Nixon in China: John Adams's opera is based on President Nixon's 1972 trip to China.

Angle between a clock's hands at....3:15: At 3:15 the minute hand sits on 3, while the hour hand has crept a quarter of the way toward 4, leaving a small gap.
Angle between a clock's hands at....9:45: At 9:45 the hour hand is three-quarters of the way from 9 to 10, nearly lining up with the minute hand at 9.
Angle between a clock's hands at....1:00: At one o'clock, the hands sit one number apart, and each number on a clock face spans 30 degrees.
Angle between a clock's hands at....2:00: At two o'clock the hands are two numbers apart, and the angle between them is 60 degrees.
Angle between a clock's hands at....12:15: At 12:15 the minute hand is at 3 while the hour hand is just past 12, which leaves slightly under a right angle.
Angle between a clock's hands at....3:00: At exactly 3:00 or 9:00 the hands form a right angle, the same corner as a square, one quarter of the clock face.
Angle between a clock's hands at....4:00: Four o'clock gives a 120-degree angle, equal to the corners of a regular hexagon's interior angle.
Angle between a clock's hands at....5:00: At five o'clock the angle is 150 degrees, close to the straight line the clock hands form at six.
Angle between a clock's hands at....12:30: At half past twelve the hour hand has moved halfway to 1, so the angle is not exactly 180 degrees.
Angle between a clock's hands at....6:00: At six o'clock the hands point in opposite directions, forming a straight line of 180 degrees.

When these civilizations collapsed or va.Indus Valley cities decline: Cities such as Mohenjo-daro had grid streets and drains; shifting monsoons likely drove their decline, and their script is still undeciphered.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Minoan palaces fall: Crete's palace of Knossos inspired the legend of the Minotaur's labyrinth; Mycenaeans gained control as the palaces fell.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Late Bronze Age collapse: Within decades, Egyptian, Hittite and Mycenaean powers were shaken by earthquakes, famine and the mysterious 'Sea Peoples'.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Olmec heartland abandoned: Their huge carved stone heads, weighing many tons, were moved long distances; the Olmec are called Mesoamerica's mother culture.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Nabataea annexed by Rome: Rome annexed the kingdom whose capital Petra, a rose-red city carved into canyon rock in Jordan, is a famed ruin.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Teotihuacan burned: Its Pyramid of the Sun was among the biggest in the Americas; who burned its ceremonial center is still debated.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Classic Maya collapse: Southern lowland cities were abandoned, likely from drought, war and land overuse, but Maya people never vanished.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Chaco Canyon abandoned: Ancestral Puebloans built great houses like Pueblo Bonito in New Mexico, aligned with the sun and moon, before drought forced them out.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Cahokia abandoned: Near modern St. Louis, it was the largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, with a 30-metre mound called Monks Mound.
When these civilizations collapsed or va.Angkor sacked: Forces from Ayutthaya sacked the Khmer capital, though the great temple Angkor Wat never fully left use.

Deepest lakes in the United States.Great Salt Lake: Saltier than the ocean, it's shallow enough that it shrinks in droughts, and it's home to brine shrimp and flies.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Erie: The shallowest of the Great Lakes, it freezes over more often than the others and grows big waves quickly.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Champlain: Straddling New York, Vermont and Quebec, it's said to be home to a monster nicknamed Champ.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Ontario: The smallest of the Great Lakes by area, it flows over Niagara Falls on the way to the Atlantic.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Michigan: The only Great Lake entirely within the US, it's connected to Lake Huron, and the two are hydrologically one lake.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Pend Oreille: Idaho's lake is used by the US Navy for testing submarine stealth technology, and it was a World War II training site.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Superior: The largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, it is known for rarely giving up its drowned.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Chelan: Washington's glacier-carved lake stretches about 50 miles, and the fjord-like basin is among the deepest in the country.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Lake Tahoe: Straddling California and Nevada, it is famed for clear blue water, and its depth makes it among the deepest lakes in North America.
Deepest lakes in the United States.Crater Lake: Formed in the collapsed crater of a volcano, Mount Mazama, it is the deepest lake in the US, and no river flows into it.

Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Sepak takraw: This Southeast Asian game is volleyball played with the feet, using a rattan ball and acrobatic overhead kicks.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Curling: Teammates are lead, second, third and skip, and the sport is nicknamed the roaring game for the sound of stones on ice.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Roller derby: Four blockers and one jammer skate for each team at a time, in a sport born on banked tracks.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Underwater hockey: Players push a puck along the pool floor with short sticks, wearing snorkels, and the sport was invented in the 1950s as a training game for divers.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Kabaddi: A raider must tag opponents and hold one breath while chanting 'kabaddi' as he returns to his side.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Korfball: A Dutch teacher, Nico Broekhuysen, invented it in 1902, and each team must have four men and four women.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Softball: It was invented in Chicago in 1887 as an indoor version of baseball, played with a boxing glove and a broom handle.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Bandy: Played on ice, the sport is like football on skates with sticks, and it is hugely popular in Russia and Sweden.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Rugby league: It split from the 15-player union game in 1895 over whether players should be paid for missing work.
Players per side in lesser-known team sp.Hurling: The sliotar, a hard leather ball, can fly faster than 100 km/h in one of the fastest field games.

How many strings each instrument has.Erhu: The bow hair of the Chinese fiddle is threaded between its two strings, so it can never be taken off the instrument.
How many strings each instrument has.Balalaika: This triangular Russian instrument usually has three strings, two of them tuned to the same note.
How many strings each instrument has.Violin: Violin strings are tuned in perfect fifths: G, D, A and E, and the hollow body gives its tone its sweetness.
How many strings each instrument has.Banjo (standard): The short fifth string, set up near the neck's fifth fret, is played by the thumb and gives the instrument its trademark drone.
How many strings each instrument has.Guitar: Spanish luthier Antonio de Torres shaped the modern six-string classical guitar in the 1800s, and designs have barely changed since.
How many strings each instrument has.Mandolin: Its eight strings come in four pairs, tuned exactly like a violin's, so a violinist can pick it up easily.
How many strings each instrument has.Twelve-string guitar: It uses six pairs of strings, and the doubling creates a shimmering chime that folk and rock players loved in the 1960s.
How many strings each instrument has.Koto: The Japanese zither's 13 strings sit over movable bridges, and players pluck them with picks worn on the fingers.
How many strings each instrument has.Concert harp: Its 47 strings are color-coded: C strings red and F strings black or dark blue, so players can find their place at a glance.
How many strings each instrument has.Grand piano: The strings under a grand piano's lid pull on the frame with a tension of many tons, and most notes use three strings at once.

Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Papin's steam digester: Denis Papin's forerunner of the pressure cooker had a safety valve; he showed it by softening bones.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Tin can: Peter Durand patented it in 1810, yet nobody invented a proper opener for nearly 50 years, so people used hammers and chisels.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Can opener: Ezra Warner's opener had a blade and a guard, and was so dangerous that stores sometimes opened cans for customers.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Dishwasher (Cochrane): Josephine Cochrane, a wealthy socialite, built one after servants kept chipping her fine china.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Paper coffee filter: Melitta Bentz, a German homemaker, punched holes in a brass pot and lined it with blotting paper from her son's schoolbook.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Pop-up toaster: Charles Strite designed it for restaurants tired of burnt toast; models for homes followed in 1926.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Waring Blendor: Bandleader Fred Waring financed it, and it was first sold to bars and soda fountains.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Tupperware: Earl Tupper adapted polyethylene scrap into airtight containers, which took off through home sales parties.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Instant noodles: Momofuku Ando created Chicken Ramen in Japan, inspired by postwar hunger and the lines at noodle stalls.
Kitchen inventions, oldest to newest.Cuisinart food processor: Carl Sontheimer adapted a French commercial machine for home cooks, and Julia Child helped make it famous in the United States.

Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Fry's chocolate bar: This Bristol firm made the first mass-produced chocolate bar meant for eating, not drinking.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Milk chocolate (Peter): Daniel Peter of Switzerland made it with milk powder supplied by his neighbour, Henri Nestlé.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Saccharin: Chemist Constantin Fahlberg noticed a sweet taste on his hands after lab work, and discovered this by accident.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Cotton candy machine: A dentist and a confectioner patented the machine, and it became a fairground classic after being shown at the 1904 World's Fair.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Popsicle: Eleven-year-old Frank Epperson reportedly invented it by leaving a stirring stick in soda on a cold night.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Gummy bears: Hans Riegel of Haribo in Bonn created them as 'dancing bears', inspired by trained bears at fairs.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Mars bar: Forrest Mars launched it in Slough, England, after learning confectionery from Swiss makers.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.M&M's: Named for Forrest Mars and Bruce Murrie, it was reportedly inspired by soldiers eating candy-coated chocolate in Spain.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Chupa Chups: The Spanish lollipop's daisy logo was designed by the artist Salvador Dalí.
Sweet inventions, oldest to newest.Aspartame: Chemist James Schlatter found it by accident while working on an ulcer drug; it is about 200 times sweeter than sugar.

When these tech words were coined.Television: Television comes from Greek tele, far, and Latin visio, sight. It was first used at the 1900 Paris Exposition.
When these tech words were coined.Robot: Robot comes from the Czech robota, meaning forced labor, and first appeared in Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R.
When these tech words were coined.Transistor: Transistor is a blend of transfer and resistor. It was invented at Bell Labs in 1947 and replaced the bulky vacuum tube.
When these tech words were coined.Byte: Werner Buchholz coined byte, and deliberately changed the spelling from bite to avoid confusion with bit.
When these tech words were coined.Laser: Laser stands for light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation, and Theodore Maiman built the first working one in 1960.
When these tech words were coined.Internet: Internet was shortened from internetworking in a 1974 paper by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn, who designed TCP.
When these tech words were coined.Blog: Blog comes from weblog. Programmer Peter Merholz joked about pronouncing it we blog, and the short form took off.
When these tech words were coined.Selfie: Selfie came out of Australia, where it appeared in an online forum post. It was chosen as Oxford's word of the year in 2013.
When these tech words were coined.Podcast: Podcast mixes iPod and broadcast, though podcasts don't need an iPod at all. Journalist Ben Hammersley suggested the word.
When these tech words were coined.Hashtag: Chris Messina proposed using the pound sign to group topics on Twitter. The word hashtag was named in 2007 and quickly became universal.

The number hiding in each word's origin.Monopoly: Monopoly comes from Greek words for one and to sell, meaning a single seller controlling a market. The board game was meant to teach the dangers of that.
The number hiding in each word's origin.Binoculars: Binoculars come from Latin words meaning "two" and "eye." The first modern ones used prisms to fold the light path.
The number hiding in each word's origin.Trivia: Trivia comes from Latin for "three roads," a crossroads where idle chatter was exchanged. Over time the meaning shrank to minor facts.
The number hiding in each word's origin.Quintessence: Quintessence was the "fifth essence" of ancient and medieval thought, beyond earth, air, fire and water. It was thought to make up the heavens.
The number hiding in each word's origin.Sextant: A sextant measures angles up to a sixth of a circle, which is 60 degrees. Sailors used it for centuries to find their latitude.
The number hiding in each word's origin.September: September was the seventh month in the ancient Roman calendar, which began in March. It kept its name after the calendar changed.
The number hiding in each word's origin.Octopus: The octopus's name literally means "eight foot" in Greek. It also has three hearts and blue blood.
The number hiding in each word's origin.November: November got its name as the ninth month of the old Roman year. January and February were added later, pushing it to eleventh.
The number hiding in each word's origin.Decimate: Decimation was a Roman army punishment, in which one in every ten soldiers was killed. Today people use it to mean massive destruction.
The number hiding in each word's origin.Quarantine: Venice kept arriving ships waiting for forty days, quaranta giorni, to guard against the plague. The word came from that rule.

Musical instruments, by invention.Bone flute: Made from a vulture's wing bone in a cave in Germany, it's around 40,000 years old. It is among the oldest known instruments.
Musical instruments, by invention.Lyres of Ur: Found in a royal cemetery of Ur in modern Iraq, they have gold and shell decoration. One has the head of a bull.
Musical instruments, by invention.Water organ (hydraulis): Ctesibius of Alexandria invented it, and water pressure steadied the air flow. It's the forerunner of the pipe organ.
Musical instruments, by invention.Violin: Andrea Amati's workshop in Cremona produced the earliest known violins. Later makers like Stradivari perfected them.
Musical instruments, by invention.Piano: Bartolomeo Cristofori of Florence built it so that keys could play soft or loud, giving it its full name "pianoforte." Earlier keyboards couldn't.
Musical instruments, by invention.Accordion: The accordion was patented in Vienna in 1829. Its reeds sound when bellows push air through them.
Musical instruments, by invention.Saxophone: Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax patented his invention in 1846. It is made of brass but played with a reed, and became a jazz icon.
Musical instruments, by invention.Theremin: Played without touching it, Léon Theremin's instrument senses the player's hands near two antennas. It's the eerie sound of old sci-fi films.
Musical instruments, by invention.Electric guitar: The first one, nicknamed the "Frying Pan," was made by Rickenbacker. It was a lap steel guitar rather than the shape we know.
Musical instruments, by invention.Moog synthesizer: Robert Moog's synthesizer reached the mainstream with Wendy Carlos's Switched-On Bach in 1968. It made electronic music popular.

When these medieval rulers died.Attila the Hun: He reportedly died on his wedding night in 453 from a nosebleed, according to the historian Priscus.
When these medieval rulers died.Theodoric the Great: The Ostrogoth king ruled Italy, and was educated as a youth in Constantinople.
When these medieval rulers died.Justinian I: He codified Roman law and built Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.
When these medieval rulers died.Charlemagne: Crowned emperor by the pope on Christmas Day, 800.
When these medieval rulers died.Alfred the Great: The only English king called 'the Great'; the legend of the burnt cakes is told about him.
When these medieval rulers died.William the Conqueror: He commissioned the Domesday Book in 1086, surveying all England.
When these medieval rulers died.Saladin: A Kurdish ruler who retook Jerusalem in 1187, and who was respected even by his Crusader foes.
When these medieval rulers died.Genghis Khan: His empire became the largest contiguous land empire in history under his successors.
When these medieval rulers died.Kublai Khan: Founder of the Yuan dynasty, he hosted Marco Polo, as the tale goes.
When these medieval rulers died.Tamerlane: Known as Timur the Lame, he died on the way to invade China.

Epidemics and pandemics through history.Plague of Justinian: The first recorded pandemic of bubonic plague hit Constantinople hard, and it recurred across the Mediterranean for two centuries.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.Black Death: It killed perhaps a third or more of Europe's people, and reshaped wages, labor and society.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.Great Plague of London: Samuel Pepys wrote about it in his diary, and the Great Fire of London followed the next year.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.Broad Street cholera: John Snow mapped the cases and had a pump handle removed, which helped found modern epidemiology.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.Spanish flu: It didn't start in Spain; neutral Spain simply reported freely during the war, so it got the name.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.Asian flu: The H2N2 flu is thought to have killed one to two million people, and a vaccine was developed within months.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.AIDS first recognized: The CDC first reported unusual cases in June 1981; the cause was identified within two years as HIV.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.SARS: The first new coronavirus scare of the century was contained within months, which seemed to show that outbreaks could be stopped.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.Swine flu: H1N1 emerged in Mexico, and was a descendant of the virus of 1918, which had circulated in pigs for decades.
Epidemics and pandemics through history.COVID-19: mRNA vaccines were developed in under a year, a technology that grew from decades of earlier research.

When these Americas nations became indep.Paraguay: It declared independence in 1811, then lived under the dictator José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia; most people speak Guaraní alongside Spanish.
When these Americas nations became indep.Argentina: Independence was declared at Tucumán on 9 July 1816, which is still the national holiday.
When these Americas nations became indep.Chile: After San Martín's army crossed the Andes, Bernardo O'Higgins formally declared independence in 1818.
When these Americas nations became indep.Mexico: A priest's 1810 'Grito de Dolores' began a decade-long war that ended in 1821.
When these Americas nations became indep.Bolivia: Named for Simón Bolívar; its capital arrangement is unusual, since Sucre is the constitutional capital and La Paz seats the government.
When these Americas nations became indep.Dominican Republic: It won independence in 1844 from Haiti, not from Spain; Spain even took it back briefly from 1861 to 1865.
When these Americas nations became indep.Panama: It broke from Colombia in 1903 with US backing, clearing the way for the canal that opened in 1914.
When these Americas nations became indep.Jamaica: Independence Day, 6 August, brings parades and festivals in the national colors of black, green and gold.
When these Americas nations became indep.Suriname: It is the only independent South American country where Dutch is the official language.
When these Americas nations became indep.Belize: It was British Honduras until 1973, and was the last mainland American colony to win independence.

When in the year these events happen.Australian Open: The first Grand Slam of the year is in Melbourne in midsummer, and extreme heat can pause play.
When in the year these events happen.Super Bowl: Held in February, it is numbered with Roman numerals and draws one of the biggest TV audiences in America.
When in the year these events happen.Cheltenham Festival: The Gold Cup draws huge crowds of Irish fans to the Gloucestershire racecourse every March.
When in the year these events happen.The Masters: Golf's first major is at Augusta National, the same course since 1934, and the winner gets a green jacket.
When in the year these events happen.Kentucky Derby: The 'most exciting two minutes in sports' takes place at Churchill Downs on the first Saturday in May.
When in the year these events happen.Tour de France: The leader wears yellow because the sponsoring newspaper L'Auto was printed on yellow paper.
When in the year these events happen.Little League World Series: The Williamsport, Pennsylvania tournament has been held since 1947, drawing kids from all over the world.
When in the year these events happen.US Open tennis finals: The finals end at Flushing Meadows, home to Arthur Ashe Stadium, the largest tennis stadium in the world.
When in the year these events happen.New York City Marathon: Running through all five boroughs on the first Sunday of November, it is the world's biggest marathon.
When in the year these events happen.Sydney to Hobart yacht race: The yacht race sets sail on Boxing Day, and runs about 630 nautical miles across the rough Bass Strait.

Peter Pan, in story order.Peter loses his shadow: J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan debuted as a play in 1904, and the novel followed in 1911.
Peter Pan, in story order.Wendy sews on his shadow: The name Wendy was rare before Barrie, and the story helped popularise it.
Peter Pan, in story order.Fairy dust and happy thoughts: In Barrie's play the audience was asked to clap to save Tinker Bell, a famous interactive moment.
Peter Pan, in story order.Flying off to Neverland: Second star to the right and straight on till morning is the way to Neverland in Barrie's story.
Peter Pan, in story order.Meeting the Lost Boys: The Lost Boys are children who fell out of their prams, and Neverland is where Peter looks after them.
Peter Pan, in story order.Rescuing Tiger Lily: Tiger Lily's portrayal has been criticised as a stereotype, and recent adaptations rework her character.
Peter Pan, in story order.Hook captures the children: In Barrie's text Captain Hook went to Eton, which he treats as the mark of a gentleman.
Peter Pan, in story order.Peter duels Hook on the ship: Peter says To die would be an awfully big adventure, one of Barrie's most quoted lines.
Peter Pan, in story order.The crocodile chases Hook: Tick-Tock the crocodile swallowed Hook's hand and a clock, and the ticking warns him of its approach.
Peter Pan, in story order.The children fly home: Barrie gave the rights to Peter Pan to Great Ormond Street Hospital in London in 1929.

Albert Einstein's life.Born in Ulm: Born in Ulm, in the kingdom of Württemberg, he moved with his family to Munich as an infant.
Albert Einstein's life.Starts at the patent office: After failing to find a teaching post, he worked as a patent clerk in Bern, evaluating electrical inventions.
Albert Einstein's life.Miracle year papers: He published four groundbreaking papers within months, covering the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and E equals mc squared.
Albert Einstein's life.General relativity: His theory described gravity as the curving of space and time, and it was confirmed by a 1919 solar eclipse.
Albert Einstein's life.Nobel Prize: His Nobel was awarded for the photoelectric effect, not relativity, which the committee considered too controversial at the time.
Albert Einstein's life.Leaves Germany for good: Einstein was visiting the US when the Nazis took power, and he never returned to Germany, settling at Princeton.
Albert Einstein's life.Letter to Roosevelt: Signed by Einstein but largely drafted by Leo Szilard, the letter warned that Germany might build an atomic bomb.
Albert Einstein's life.Becomes a US citizen: He kept his Swiss citizenship too, and he had earlier renounced his German citizenship as a young man.
Albert Einstein's life.Offered Israel's presidency: He declined, saying he lacked 'the natural aptitude and the experience to deal properly with people'.
Albert Einstein's life.Dies in Princeton: He died of a burst aortic aneurysm, and his brain was removed and preserved without his family's initial consent.
